title: India Open Their T20 World Cup Against Pakistan on Saturday. Here Is Everything You Need to Know.
excerpt: The ICC Women's T20 World Cup begins Thursday in England with 12 teams across six venues. India's campaign starts at Edgbaston with a blockbuster group stage draw.
body:
Four days from now, the ICC Women's T20 World Cup begins in England. Twelve teams. Six venues. Twenty-three days. And for Harmanpreet Kaur's India, the tournament opens with the most high-profile fixture possible: India versus Pakistan, at Edgbaston, on Saturday, June 14.

India arrive in England as reigning 50-over World Cup champions and recent T20I series participants against England, where they lost the series but gained clarity about their best XI. The question is no longer whether this squad has talent. It is whether that talent can hold together in the tournament that has eluded them the longest.

## India's Squad

Harmanpreet Kaur leads a 15-member squad that blends experience with emerging firepower:

**Batters:** Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Bharti Fulmali, Yastika Bhatia

**All-rounders:** Deepti Sharma, Shree Charani, Nandani Sharma

**Wicketkeeper:** Richa Ghosh

**Bowlers:** Arundhati Reddy, Renuka Singh, Kranti Gaud, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav

Nandani Sharma, who took a hat-trick in only her second WPL match and earned her India debut five weeks later, is the squad's breakout pick. Yastika Bhatia's return after injury adds depth to the middle order. Renuka Singh's pace and Deepti Sharma's off-spin give India a balanced attack, though the absence of a second frontline pacer beyond Renuka remains a concern.

## The Group: A Brutal Draw

India are in Group 1, which also includes Australia, South Africa, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the Netherlands. It is, by any measure, the tougher group. Australia are the defending champions from 2024 (though now led by Sophie Molineux after roster changes). South Africa under Laura Wolvaardt are one of the most consistent sides in women's cricket. Pakistan, captained by Fatima Sana, have improved rapidly.

India must finish in the top four of their group to reach the semi-finals.

## India's Schedule

| Date | Match | Venue | Time (BST / IST) |
|------|-------|-------|-------------------|
| June 14 | **India vs Pakistan** | Edgbaston, Birmingham | 2:30 PM / 7:00 PM |
| June 17 | India vs Netherlands | Headingley, Leeds | 2:30 PM / 7:00 PM |
| June 21 | South Africa vs India | Old Trafford, Manchester | 2:30 PM / 7:00 PM |
| June 25 | India vs Bangladesh | Old Trafford, Manchester | 2:30 PM / 7:00 PM |
| June 28 | Australia vs India | Lord's, London | 2:30 PM / 7:00 PM |

The group stage finale against Australia at Lord's on June 28 could decide both semi-final spots.

## Where to Watch

- **India, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Maldives:** Star Sports (TV) and JioHotstar (streaming)
- **United States and Canada:** Willow TV
- **United Kingdom:** Sky Sports
- **Australia:** Prime Video
- **Pakistan:** PTV Sports, Geo Super, and Myco
- **Global:** ICC.tv (territories without a dedicated broadcaster)

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

The tournament is being held across six English venues — Edgbaston, Headingley, Old Trafford, Lord's, The Oval, and the Hampshire Bowl — all accessible cities for the UK's 1.8 million-strong Indian diaspora. The India-Pakistan match at Edgbaston on June 14 is expected to sell out. For NRIs in Birmingham, Leeds, Manchester, and London, this is a rare chance to watch India's women play live in a global tournament on home soil.

Semi-finals are on June 30 and July 1 at The Oval and Lord's. The final is at Lord's on July 5.

## The Contenders

**Australia** remain the benchmark. Ellyse Perry at 35 is playing what may be her final World Cup. Ashleigh Gardner's all-round ability and Megan Schutt's pace make them formidable.

**England**, playing at home, have Nat Sciver-Brunt, Sophie Ecclestone, and the crowd behind them. They are in Group 2 with New Zealand, West Indies, Sri Lanka, Ireland, and Scotland — a kinder draw.

**South Africa** have been the most consistent side in ICC events without winning one. Wolvaardt's captaincy and Marizanne Kapp's experience make them dangerous.

**India** have the batting to beat anyone. Mandhana and Shafali at the top can take any attack apart. But India's T20 World Cup history is a story of near-misses — the 2020 final loss to Australia remains fresh — and this squad knows that talent alone has never been enough.

The tournament opens on Thursday, June 12, with England against Sri Lanka at Edgbaston. India's campaign begins two days later.

*Forty-eight hours of waiting. Then Pakistan.*
